name: CUPIDO 2
question: Does adding a midurethral sling to vaginal prolapse repair improve continence in women with occult stress urinary incontinence?

arms.label: Vaginal prolapse repair with a midurethral sling

design.population: Stress-continent women with symptomatic stage II or greater pelvic organ prolapse and stress leakage demonstrated only after prolapse reduction at 13 Dutch teaching hospitals.
design.description: Multicenter, unblinded randomized superiority trial with parallel cohort
design.locator: Primary report, pp 43–46, Methods and Figure 1

verdictNote: Continence improved, while overall postoperative complications were more frequent with a sling.
takeaway: In women with occult stress incontinence, adding a midurethral sling to vaginal prolapse repair increased reported absence of stress incontinence at 12 months (86% versus 48%); 6 of 47 controls later received a sling, while overall complications were more frequent with concomitant surgery.

reports.label: Randomized 12-month report
reports.citation: van der Ploeg JM, Oude Rengerink K, van der Steen A, et al. "Vaginal prolapse repair with or without a midurethral sling in women with genital prolapse and occult stress urinary incontinence: a randomized trial." *Int Urogynecol J.* 2016;27(7):1029-1038. doi:10.1007/s00192-015-2924-1
reports.followUpLocator: Primary report, pp 42, 44, Methods and abstract

results.measure: No stress or urgency incontinence symptoms on UDI at 12 months
results.note: The article prints 76% versus 38%; 18/46 equals 39.1%, and the published RR agrees with the fractions.
results.locator: Primary report, p 48, Table 2; p 44, Outcome measures and power calculation

results.measure: No stress incontinence symptoms on UDI at 12 months
results.note: Reported as 86% versus 48% in the article.

results.endpoint: Additional treatment for stress urinary incontinence
results.measure: Any SUI treatment during the first postoperative year
results.note: Control treatments: pelvic floor muscle training only in 4, sling only in 4, and sling after training in 2; no separate P value reported.
results.locator: Primary report, pp 44, 48, Outcome measures and Table 2 footnote d

results.measure: Any OAB treatment during the first postoperative year
results.note: Reported as 10% versus 6%; no significant difference described.
results.locator: Primary report, pp 44, 48–49, Outcome measures, Table 2 and Bladder storage

results.measure: Bothersome SUI or positive stress test at 12 months, or any SUI treatment during the first postoperative year
results.note: The composite retains women treated for SUI as events.
results.locator: Primary report, pp 44, 48, Outcome measures and Table 2 footnote e

results.measure: Much or very much improved at 12 months
results.note: No difference in global improvement or quality of life was reported.
results.locator: Primary report, pp 50–51, Table 4 and Symptom bother and quality of life

harms.label: Any postoperative complication during the first year
harms.note: RR 2.73 (95% CI 1.35–5.55); severity graded with the Accordion system.

harms.label: Severe complication
harms.note: Difference was not statistically significant; trial was underpowered for uncommon harms.

harms.label: Vaginal tape perforation or exposure
harms.locator: Primary report, pp 49–50, Complications and Table 3
harms.note: One insertion perforation, one asymptomatic exposure, and one symptomatic exposure requiring partial excision. Table 3 separates two mild events and one severe exposure.

harms.label: Postoperative urinary tract infection
harms.note: Moderate complication; difference was not statistically significant.

harms.label: Incomplete emptying with catheterization beyond one week
harms.locator: Primary report, p 50, Table 3 and footnote b
harms.note: Indwelling or intermittent catheterization; difference was not statistically significant.

delivery.label: Vaginal prolapse operations
delivery.value: Anterior repair: 37/43 (86%) versus 41/47 (87%); apical repair: 32/43 (74%) versus 31/47 (66%); posterior repair: 28/43 (65%) versus 22/47 (47%).

delivery.label: Sling placement and route
delivery.value: 41/43 (95%) assigned women received a sling after prolapse correction: 38 transobturator and 3 retropubic; one refused and one sling was omitted.
delivery.locator: Primary report, pp 44–46, Surgery and Results; Figure 1

delivery.label: Secondary sling in the prolapse-only group
delivery.locator: Primary report, pp 46–48, Urinary outcome and Table 2 footnote d
delivery.note: Six control patients underwent a sling for de novo SUI during the first postoperative year.

reports.label: Office testing and urodynamics analysis
reports.citation: van der Ploeg JM, Zwolsman SE, Posthuma S, et al. "The predictive value of demonstrable stress incontinence during basic office evaluation and urodynamics in women without symptomatic urinary incontinence undergoing vaginal prolapse surgery." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2018;37(3):1011-1018. doi:10.1002/nau.23384
reports.followUpLocator: Secondary report, pp 58–60, Abstract and Methods

results.endpoint: Postoperative SUI by office stress test
results.measure: Bothersome SUI or treatment after prolapse-only repair; pooled CUPIDO 1/2 observational subset
results.note: Office leakage: 9/32 (28.1%) developed postoperative SUI; no office leakage: 7/140 (5.0%). These groups are not the randomized sling arms.
results.locator: Secondary report, pp 61, 64–65, Results and Tables 2–3

results.measure: Urodynamics after a negative office test in a nonrandomized subset
results.note: Among 66 office-negative women who underwent urodynamics, postoperative SUI occurred in 1/15 (6.7%) with urodynamic leakage and 3/51 (5.9%) without it; test performance did not improve.
results.locator: Secondary report, pp 61, 64–65, Results and Tables 2–3

relations.note: Same Dutch CUPIDO program and vaginal sling comparison; CUPIDO 1 enrolled women with overt SUI.
